words.en: causing fear to all the worlds
words.g: n. nom. sg.; compound (see Samāsa); qualifies युद्धम्

sandhi.note: Visarga before t becomes s (शस्त्रैस्तथा); ā + a → ā (तथास्त्रैः); visarga before c becomes s and then ś (अस्त्रैश्च); a + e → ai (चैव).
Before a sibilant the visarga may stay as it is; the Gita Press keeps it.
Visarga after o before the voiced y is r; final t becomes d before the voiced bh.

samasa.type: upapada tatpuruṣa (कर from √कृ with a kṛt affix; भय takes the augment m, भयम्-कर), containing a ṣaṣṭhī tatpuruṣa (सर्वलोकभय) and a karmadhāraya (सर्वलोक = सर्वे लोकाः)
samasa.literal: making the fear of all the worlds

morph.note: Root aorist of √भू: ‘was, came about’. Used beside the perfect as a narrative past.
In compounds of the type भयङ्कर the first member keeps an inserted m (भयम्-कर, written भयङ्कर), as in प्रियंवद, अरिंदम.

mantras.anvaya: शरवर्षैः शितैः शस्त्रैः तथा च एव दारुणैः अस्त्रैः तयोः सर्वलोकभयङ्करं युद्धं भूयः अभूत्।
mantras.anvaya_en: Instruments (शरवर्षैः, शस्त्रैः, अस्त्रैः, each with its adjective), the genitive तयोः, and the main clause युद्धं भूयः अभूत् with the predicate adjective सर्वलोकभयङ्करम्.
mantras.lit: With showers of arrows, with sharp weapons, and likewise with terrible missiles too, the battle of the two took place again, causing fear to all the worlds.
mantras.tr: With volleys of arrows, keen-edged weapons and fearsome missiles the battle between them raged on, terrifying all the worlds.

comm.t: The duel is fought first with weapons at a distance. The pair शस्त्र / अस्त्र is the usual Epic distinction: weapons held in the hand and missiles that are thrown or charged with power (the divine astras of the next verse). For the second half of the first line other witnesses read तथा चास्त्रैः सुदारुणैः (GRETIL, Freund) for the Gita Press तथास्त्रैश्चैव दारुणैः; the sense, ‘and with (very) terrible missiles’, is the same. The Gita Press reading is kept.

flags.uncertain: Variant (corrections.json, status ‘Textual Verification Required’): तथा चास्त्रैः सुदारुणैः for तथास्त्रैश्चैव दारुणैः (GRETIL, Freund). The Gita Press reading is analysed.

samasa.vigraha: तेषां प्रतीघातः तत्प्रतीघातः; तत्प्रतीघातस्य कर्तॄणि, तैः
samasa.type: ṣaṣṭhī tatpuruṣa (kṛdyoga: कर्तृ governs its object in the genitive), containing a ṣaṣṭhī tatpuruṣa (तत्प्रतीघात)
samasa.literal: with makers of the repulse of those
samasa.sense: with counter-weapons that strike them down

morph.note: Perfect middle of √मुच्, reduplicated मु-मुच्-ए. The middle is common in the Epic for ‘discharge (one’s weapons)’.
Perfect of √भञ्ज् with reduplication ब-भञ्ज्; the nasal of the root is kept.
प्रतीघात is प्रति + घात (√हन् + घञ्) with the prefix lengthened, as often before a घञ् derivative. कर्तृ is an agent noun (tṛc), here neuter instrumental plural agreeing with an understood अस्त्रैः.

mantras.anvaya: अथ अम्बिका यानि दिव्यानि अस्त्राणि शतशः मुमुचे, तानि दैत्येन्द्रः तत्प्रतीघातकर्तृभिः (अस्त्रैः) बभञ्ज।
mantras.anvaya_en: A relative clause (यानि … मुमुचे) names the object; the main clause (तानि … बभञ्ज) has its instrument in तत्प्रतीघातकर्तृभिः.
mantras.lit: The divine missiles which Ambikā then released by hundreds — those the lord of the Daityas shattered with (weapons) that effect the counter-blow to them.
mantras.tr: The divine missiles Ambikā loosed by the hundred, the Daitya king shattered with counter-weapons.

comm.t: The first exchange: the Goddess’s divine astras are met and broken by Śumbha’s counter-weapons. He is a worthy opponent; the narrative does not make the victory easy.

Lalitā Sahasranāma (Brahmāṇḍa Purāṇa) describes the same kind of duel in its own war story, naming the Goddess भण्डासुरेन्द्रनिर्मुक्तशस्त्रप्रत्यस्त्रवर्षिणी (79), ‘she who rains counter-weapons against the weapons released by Bhaṇḍāsura’. There it is the Goddess who counters; here, for a moment, it is the demon.

samasa.literal: with (means) of which the uttering of a fierce hum is the first
samasa.sense: by fierce cries of ‘hum’ and such means

morph.note: Past passive participle of √मुच् with the agent तेन in the instrumental: ‘released by him’.
Instrumental of manner: ‘in play’. The Goddess’s acts are often said to be done in sport (लीला), without effort.

mantras.anvaya: परमेश्वरी च तेन मुक्तानि दिव्यानि अस्त्राणि उग्रहुङ्कारोच्चारणादिभिः लीलया एव बभञ्ज।
mantras.anvaya_en: Subject परमेश्वरी, verb बभञ्ज, object अस्त्राणि with two qualifiers (मुक्तानि तेन, दिव्यानि), and two instrumentals: लीलया (manner) and उग्रहुङ्कारोच्चारणादिभिः (means).
mantras.lit: And the supreme Sovereign broke the divine missiles released by him, just in play, with utterances of a fierce ‘hum’ and the like.
mantras.tr: And the divine missiles he released, the supreme Goddess broke as if in play, with a fierce cry of ‘hum’ and other such means.

comm.t: The Goddess’s answer to 10.12: where Śumbha needed counter-weapons, she needs only a sound. The हुङ्कार has done this before — it laid low Mahiṣa’s spear (3.12) and burned Dhūmralocana to ashes (6.13).
In the Śākta tradition the hum-sound is the Goddess’s own power of speech used as a weapon; the verse sets lordship (परमेश्वरी) beside play (लीलया): the supreme ruler acts without effort.
Lalitā Sahasranāma (Brahmāṇḍa Purāṇa) also names her परमेश्वरी (396), and calls her लीलाविनोदिनी (966), ‘she who delights in play’. The names express a shared Śākta idea; the texts are separate.

sandhi.note: Visarga after ai before the voiced d is sounded as r; the m of देवीम् joins the following vowel.
सः before a becomes so and the a is elided (avagraha).
Visarga before c becomes ś (धनुश्चिच्छेद); a + i → e (चेषुभिः).

samasa.alt: Also possible: तत् as a separate adverb, ‘therefore’, with कुपिता ‘angered’; the Gita Press prints the two together, and the compound reading is taken here. The sense is the same.

morph.note: Imperfect middle of the causative छादय-: the augment अ merges with the prefix आ (आ + अ → आ), and छ is doubled after the prefix आ, as it always is after आ and मा: आ-च्छादय-त.
Perfect of √छिद्: reduplicated चि-च्छेद, with छ doubled after the short vowel (छे च, 6.1.73) and guṇa of the root.

mantras.anvaya: ततः सः असुरः शरशतैः देवीम् आच्छादयत। तत्कुपिता सा देवी अपि इषुभिः (तस्य) धनुः च चिच्छेद।
mantras.anvaya_en: Two sentences: Śumbha’s attack (शरशतैः … आच्छादयत) and the Goddess’s reply (सा … धनुः च चिच्छेद इषुभिः). च here joins the clauses; the possessive ‘his’ is supplied.
mantras.lit: Then that asura covered the Goddess with hundreds of arrows. She too, the Goddess, angered at that, cut his bow with arrows.
mantras.tr: Then the asura covered the Goddess with arrows by the hundred; and she, angered, cut his bow apart with her own arrows.

comm.t: Śumbha tries to overwhelm her with sheer numbers; the Goddess answers by cutting his bow. The sequence of 10.14–19 strips him of each weapon in turn: bow, spear, sword and shield, chariot, mace.
A modern reading: the Goddess does not answer numbers with numbers. She removes the means of attack, one at a time.

flags.uncertain: तत्कुपिता is read as a compound (तेन कुपिता); a reading तत् कुपिता, with तत् ‘thereupon’, is also possible and gives the same sense.

sandhi.note: The m of शक्तिम् joins the vowel; अथ + आददे: a + ā → ā.
i before a dissimilar vowel becomes y (अप्यस्य); the m of ताम् joins the vowel.

morph.note: Locative absolute: छिन्ने धनुषि, ‘the bow having been cut’ — the participle agrees with the locative noun and gives the circumstance of the main action.
Perfect middle of √दा with आ: reduplicated द-द्-ए. आ + √दा in the middle means ‘to take for oneself’ — the reverse of ‘give’.

mantras.anvaya: धनुषि छिन्ने (सति), दैत्येन्द्रः तथा अथ शक्तिम् आददे। देवी अस्य करे स्थितां ताम् अपि चक्रेण चिच्छेद।
mantras.anvaya_en: A locative absolute (छिन्ने धनुषि) and two main clauses: Śumbha takes up the spear; the Goddess cuts it.
mantras.lit: The bow having been cut, the lord of the Daityas then took up a spear. The Goddess cut that too, resting in his hand, with her discus.
mantras.tr: His bow cut through, the Daitya lord seized a spear; that too the Goddess cut with her discus while it was still in his hand.
mantras.tr_note: ‘while it was still in his hand’ renders अस्य करे स्थिताम्, ‘resting in his hand’.

comm.t: The second weapon goes: the spear (शक्ति) is cut before it can be thrown — while it is still ‘resting in his hand’.
A modern reading: the word शक्ति is used here of the demon’s weapon. The narrative lets ‘power’ in his hand be cut by the one who is Power itself — an irony the Sanskrit permits but does not state.
